Several haplotypes, possibly associated with tendency to develop a T helper-2 response, are associated with increased susceptibility to the development of the disease. Some breeds, including German shepherd dog, boxer, Rottweiler, Alaskan Malamutes, appear to be susceptible. Conversely, some autochthonous Mediterranean breeds (e.g., Ibizian hound)
respond with an effective cellular response and very rarely develop clinical signs.

In areas where CanL is endemic, the prevalence of infection is very high (over 50%) with seroprevalences ranging between 5% and 30%. However, less than 5% of dogs develop clinical signs. Isolated cases have been observed in non-endemic areas (Northern Europe, United States), most often in dogs that have visited areas where the disease is endemic.

During treatment with allopurinol, a low-purine diet is recommended to avoid xanthinuria and urolithiasis.

Treatment does not completely eliminate infection despite the clinical improvement. Dogs remain infected life-long. Regular examinations for early detection of disease relapses needed. Application of topical insecticides (pyrethroids) are necessary to minimize the risk of transmission to other animals.

Meglumine antimoniate 100 mg/kg SC q24h for 4–6 weeks with allopurinol 10 mg/kg PO q12h for at least 6 months. Miltefosine 2 mg/kg PO q24h (with allopurinol) instead of meglumine antimoniate: This combination appears to be less effective. The use of immunostimulants (domperidone, nucleotides) may reduce the risk of disease relapses. Treatment with allopurinol and an immunostimulant (domperidone or nucleotides) alone effective in cases of mild or moderate disease, but it is generally not effective (not recommended) in severe cases.
Meglumine antimoniate is contraindicated in patients with severe kidney disease due to potential nephrotoxicity.

Meglumine antimoniate causes pain and inflammation at injection site; vomiting and diarrhea are common side effects. Allopurinol can cause development of xanthine uroliths. Dogs on long treatment with allopurinol should be fed a low-purine diet.
Allopurinol may decrease the hepatic metabolism of azathioprine. If used concurrently the dosage of azathioprine should be reduced by one-third. Allopurinol may increase serum cyclosporine level.
